# FSM Platform v1 — Issue Index

Tracer-bullet vertical slices for the greenfield FSM GPS Field Service Management platform
(NestJS backend + React/Vite admin dashboard + RN/Expo SE mobile app). Each issue is a thin
end-to-end slice (schema → API → UI → tests). Generated by `/to-issues` from `docs/`
(priority: PRD-fsm-admin-dashboard.md → fsm-business-technical-workflow.md → backend design docs).

Triage: AFK slices are `ready-for-agent`; HITL slices (01, 03) are `ready-for-human`.
Sequence loosely follows the backend LLD phases P0–P7. "Blocked by" gives the build order.

> **Branch lineage (historical):** on 2026-06-29 the two divergent lines (`feat/fe-enterprise-ui`,
> `feat/issue-34-install-lifecycle`) were merged into `integration/fe-plus-backend` (merge `fd64150`;
> the `#71`/`#72` collision was resolved by renumbering to **`#79`/`#80`** — see
> [`../../docs/archive/HANDOFF-2026-06-29-integration.md`](../../docs/archive/HANDOFF-2026-06-29-integration.md)).
> Since then all work continued on **`feat/autoplant-integration`** (pushed to origin 2026-07-10),
> which is the current single line of development — see `docs/SYSTEM-STATE-2026-07.md` §8.

> **Convention — check status lines against `git log`/source before trusting them.** This tracker
> and the docs it links have gone stale-in-place four times: #99 (row 2, this file) and #176 marked
> done while a doc elsewhere still described them as open; the 2026-07-31 implementation audit's
> #162 line went stale three days later when #162 actually landed; #91's own "still live" status
> line undercounted how much of its schema had already shipped (`dd9846b`, Slice 1). None of these
> were wrong when written — the doc body just wasn't edited in place when reality moved past it,
> which is exactly the drift this file's own "edit in place, never fork" rule exists to prevent. A
> status line (`Status:`, `Progress:`, a row's Evidence column, a "done"/"still live" claim in prose)
> is a **hypothesis to re-check against `git log`/the current source**, not a fact to carry forward —
> especially for anything security- or auth-relevant, where a few days' staleness has already produced
> a materially wrong risk read twice (see `docs/status/mobile-readiness-2026-08.md` Phase 3).

### Mobile contract-freeze block (filed 2026-07-28 — `docs/status/mobile-backend-freeze-plan-2026-07-28.md`)

Three mobile-readiness assessments reconciled into one plan against a **stricter bar**: the backend
contract must be frozen *before* mobile starts, so that no backend change is needed mid-build. The
plan supersedes all three source documents (banners added). **Honest verdict on the bar: ~85%
achievable — four categories (field-level completeness, client-discovered error cases, offline sync
semantics, real-device performance) cannot be frozen ahead of a client.** The recommended bar is
contract-*compatibility* (versioning + additive-only + shared types + OTA) rather than
contract-*immutability*: **59–87 engineer-days vs 96–142**. §4 of the plan is the deliverable — a
34-route contract inventory with per-route STABLE/CHANGE/NEW/DECIDE verdicts, 54 error codes, and
the serialization hazards.

Six new issues (**#169–#174**); extensions appended to **#161–#167** (revised) and
**#107 #91 #84 #81 #59 #88** (plus the earlier #101/#106/#110/#147/#111/#82/#76 extensions,
corrected).

### Mobile pilot-readiness block (filed 2026-08-04 — `audit/mobile-device-readiness-2026-08-04.md` + `audit/mobile-contract-sync-audit-2026-08-04.md`)

**This block has a parent issue, unlike the two above** —
[**#197**](./issues/197-mobile-pilot-readiness-remediation-epic.md) is the pilot go/no-go owner, which
is what [#170](./issues/170-mobile-release-upgrade-mechanism.md)'s *"owner needed before pilot"* has
lacked since 2026-08-03. Read the epic first; it carries the execution order, the coverage matrix
(every audit finding ID → slice or explicit disposition), and the in-place corrections.

Four structural root causes, not a list of bugs: **(1)** mobile has no HTTP middleware layer, so every
screen hand-rolls auth and maps any failure to "Offline"; **(2)** contract types are synchronised by
convention, not types — no parity test exists anywhere; **(3)** the admin app does not consume
contracts that already ship (`GET /api/media/:id`, `/api/intraday-insertions`, the whole notification
spine — **zero** callers each), so three PRD-specified manager workflows are dead on a green backend;
**(4)** no document defines what "today" means, while three surfaces each assume a different answer.
Underneath all four: no native build has ever been produced and the one SE who can log in has no work
data.

**Decisions — ALL THREE RULED 2026-08-04, so no slice in this block is decision-blocked:**
[#198](./issues/198-decision-day-boundary-and-dispatch-clock.md) → the operating day is the **IST day**
(`Asia/Kolkata`); dispatch at **05:00 IST** default, `Asia/Kolkata` business timezone, **operator-configurable
not hardcoded**; leave dates are IST calendar days ·
[#199](./issues/199-decision-one-active-device-cross-surface.md) → **one handset + one browser** (a second
*handset* login still revokes the first), plus a distinct "signed in on another device" error code and a
short rotation grace window ·
[#200](./issues/200-decision-deferred-vs-removed-presentation.md) → day-plan changes are
**server-authoritative and restart-durable**, defer shows its return date, and a bulk rebalance gets its own
"plan being rebuilt" state.

The dispatch ruling was wider than the question, so it spawned
[**#213**](./issues/213-configurable-dispatch-schedule.md) — but **four of the five asks already exist**
(manual `POST /schedules/dispatch-run`, its OH/CSM role gate, its full MANUAL+actor audit bracket, and its
admin button). Only two gaps are real: the schedule is an env var rather than a `system_settings` entry, and
the single-in-flight guard sits on the scheduler while the manual trigger calls the run service directly —
so the path an operator uses in an emergency is the one with no concurrency guard.

Building #204 surfaced a second ruling the audits had missed entirely: the **analytics** day was still
UTC while operations moved to IST, so a ticket closed at 02:00 IST lands on today's Day Plan but in
yesterday's efficiency cube. Ruled 2026-08-04 — **move analytics to the IST day and recompute**,
accepting that recompute rewrites recorded rows (CONTEXT.md §19 addendum). Filed as
[**#214**](./issues/214-analytics-day-ist-recompute.md), which carries the part #204 could not answer:
four of the five cubes were never audited, and #214 requires a written finding on each *before*
anything is recomputed.

Admission is `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, **not** the issue's insert-and-catch: a P2002 aborts its tx (#265), `DO NOTHING` returns a row count instead, and that is what lets run row + claims + refusals share **one** rollback-able transaction — which is what makes "two cases, no third" true when the last free zone is taken mid-admission. **A defect AC-1 would not have caught:** the loser of a race re-read *live* claims after its rollback and the winner may have finalized already → `inFlight: []`, a bare 409 (intermittent, 2 of 5 runs); now reads the **latest** claim row for the zone inside the losing tx. `status` is an enum not the issue's TEXT; `contended_with_run_id` carries no FK; the response field is `zoneOutcomes` (`zones` is a count). `started_at` now means "claimed", not "processing began". CONTENDED is **not** an error (`error` stays null; status → PARTIAL). **Absorbed #252** (+#177's third column). **#261 owns the reaper** — this covers a run that unwinds, not a process that dies | M |
| 3 | [#261](./issues/261-dispatch-run-heartbeat-reaper.md) | Heartbeat + reaper + conditional finish; same fix to ingestion ledgers (folds #132) | #259 · ✅ **DONE 2026-08-23** ([`docs/progress/261-dispatch-run-heartbeat-reaper.md`](../../docs/progress/261-dispatch-run-heartbeat-reaper.md)) — **the beat is the reaper's precondition, not a refinement of it**: an age-keyed reaper eventually frees a *live* long run's zones and lets a second run in on top, which is worse than the wedge it fixes. `heartbeat_at` on all three ledgers (nullable, no default — pre-column rows fall back to `started_at`, and a test fails when that arm is removed), beaten per zone / per chunk / per master-sync stage. **`ABORTED` is a new status, not FAILED**: FAILED is about the WORK, ABORTED means nobody knows what the run did. Reaper writes run-then-claims so a death mid-reap is self-correcting. Both finalizes became `updateMany` on `status='RUNNING'` — without that the reaper *creates* zombie-resurrect on the dispatch side. ## P9 — Assign Work Console (approved UI direction [#272](./issues/272-decision-assign-work-console.md), approved 2026-08-20)

The operator approved a single manual-assignment console to replace the seven scattered surfaces that
can move work to an engineer today — none of which shows how much work exists, how much is left after
the write, or whether the chosen engineer can carry it. **#272 is the record; the design file is
authoritative** and lives in the repo at
[`docs/ui/desktop/approved-designs/assign-work-console.html`](../../docs/ui/desktop/approved-designs/assign-work-console.html)
(published copy: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/369ddf01-b727-4d9b-b086-00714480bb74). No v2
reference image covers this screen; approved designs now sit at the same authority level as the v2
set for screens the reference never drew — see `docs/agents/domain.md` § UI authority and the
`approved-designs/README.md` index. **Do not redesign the console; build it.**

**What was wrong, in one line:** every manual write in the codebase is shaped N→1 (many tickets, one
engineer, committed immediately, no preview, no residual) while the dispatcher's job is M→N.

**P9 is 6 of 6 done — #272–#277, the whole Assign Work Console is closed.** The console displays capacity and candidate order, so its
numbers must be true before they are shown: **#178** (closure clears assignment, or the load column
lies) → **#269** (the one `{committed, dailyCapacity}` payload — P9 consumes it and defines no second
counter) · **#266** (score decides nothing today at `recommender.service.ts:466`, so a rendered
candidate order would teach a false model) · **#262** (the per-SE transaction shape `assign-batch`
must match) · **#265** (clean 409s — the console multiplies concurrent manual writes) · **#250** ✅
(the dry-run seam Distribute projects through).

**#269 stays "existing pages, no redesign" and is not superseded** — it is the instrumentation this
console was written to consume.

**Two of #272's three open questions are ruled** (draft persistence — session-local; Distribute RBAC —
all managers, the same `MANAGER_ROLES` ladder as the console's own draft/commit). **The third — Device
Detail panel retired or kept as a deep-link shortcut — is still open**, but turned out not to gate #277:
that issue's actual required changes never touched `AssignSePanel`, so it shipped without needing the
ruling. Left for whoever next revisits the Device Detail panel.

Build order — **strictly sequential**; each slice is usable on its own:

## P10 — Dispatch timeline navigation (decision [#280](./issues/280-decision-dispatch-timeline-ia.md), direction approved 2026-08-24)

**Filed 2026-08-24 from the 2026-08-19 UX/navigation audits. #280 ruled the same day (R1–R10, Q4
still open and non-blocking); #281 built the same day — P10 is closed.** Audit finding **F6 (HIGH)**: *Scheduler Preview* (what the next run would do),
*Schedules* (what the current run produced) and *Dispatch Runs* (the ledger of past runs) are three
views of one dispatch timeline presented as unrelated navigation destinations — adjacent in `nav.ts`
"only because they were added in that order" — and the `Run → Zone → Batch` drill-down dead-ends at
Batch, where `seName` / `plantName` / `ticketId` are rendered but never linked.

**Distinct from P9.** P9 (#272–#277, landed `6ceaea5`) built `/assign`, the **manual** M→N assignment
surface. P10 is the **automatic** engine's own timeline — future / present / past. The two are not
merged (#280 R7).

**The hard constraint (#280 R2):** grouping and cross-linking, **not** merging. Previewing a future
run, reading the committed result, and inspecting history are three different operator questions;
collapsing them would be a worse error than the present fragmentation.

| # | Item | Scope (one line) | Prereq | Size |

Only **Q4** (commit the source audits) remains open, and it does not block #281 | — | S (docs) |

## P11 — Today's Dispatch / Crew Deck (decision [#282](./issues/282-decision-todays-dispatch-crew-deck.md), approved 2026-08-25)

**Filed 2026-08-25 from [`audit/scheduler-engine-forensics-2026-08-25.md`](../../audit/scheduler-engine-forensics-2026-08-25.md)** —
a five-part forensic investigation of the scheduler engine against its 2026-08-19 (backend) and
2026-08-19/20 (UI) baselines. Verdict: **the backend is substantially complete and correct against
the ratified #258 model; the gap is the operator surface plus a small set of named seams.** The
engine is **not** rebuilt — run machinery, tick claims, admission, heartbeat/reaper, bounded retry,
recommender, scoring, capacity, per-SE transactions, traces, Preview, DecisionTrace, the Dispatch
Runs ledger, P9 and P10's work are all reused (#282 R5).

**Why this exists:** the Crew Deck design was produced 2026-08-20 alongside #272, lived only in an
uncommitted artifact, and was lost — which is how #280 came to record "no wireframe exists" and
scope #281 to navigation only. Recovered and approved 2026-08-25. **The lesson is filed, not just
the issue:** a design that is not in `docs/ui/desktop/approved-designs/` does not exist to the next
session.

**Two operational rulings came with it (#282 R3/R4):** crashed-zone re-dispatch is **same-day,
bounded, automatic** through the normal admission path (previously a mid-run crash cost the zone its
field day); mid-day SE unavailability is **escalate-only** (nothing re-plans automatically — since
#268 retired the timeout reroute, nothing happened at all).

Build order — #283 and #284 are the spine; #285 consumes both:

## Deferred / decided-against

Decisions to **not** build, with the analysis that settled them. Unlike Next-up, nothing here is
scheduled — items move out only on new evidence.

- **Per-zone engine *configuration* (raw ZM-editable knobs) — DECIDED AGAINST (2026-07-21).**
  Analysis: [`docs/proposals/zone-engine-customization-2026-07-21.md`](../../docs/proposals/zone-engine-customization-2026-07-21.md)
  (commit `f0f3dcb`). Exposing ticket-creation / assignment-engine settings as per-zone knobs a ZM
  edits is a net-negative: the most-wanted knob (`inactivity_threshold_hours`) defines the Fleet-Uptime
  / Soft-Inactive **denominator**, so per-zone values make zones non-comparable in the very reports
  that grade them **and** let a graded ZM tune their own scorecard; `eligibility_mode` and scoring
  weights fail the same test; and it taxes the single-scalar set-based recompute hot path. Most real ZM
  wants already exist as per-instance levers (override / same-day / planner / capacity). **What we build
  instead:** legibility now → [#136](./issues/136-zone-operating-mode-visibility.md); two OH-bounded
  postures only on evidenced demand → [#137](./issues/137-per-zone-operating-postures.md) (deferred).
- **Per-zone operating postures (ZM-tunable, OH-bounded) → [#137](./issues/137-per-zone-operating-postures.md)**
  — deferred, gated on evidenced operator demand + OH sign-off (proposal §4 Approach B / §5 P2). Not
  scheduled; filed so the option isn't lost.

| 2026-07-22 | **Backend + web-app readiness for the SE mobile client — READ-ONLY assessment (no code, no issues, no design).** Answered "what must the server side become before a 1,000-device SE app can connect": traced all 52 controllers (15 expose `SERVICE_ENGINEER`), the auth/token internals, every SE mutation's retry-safety, and measured payloads + DB limits live. **Three hard blockers, none of which mobile-side engineering can work around.** (1) **An SE cannot read a ticket** — `GET /tickets/:id|/tickets|/:id/forms` are all ZM/CSM/OH-only (`tickets.controller.ts:38,70,83`), and `GET /schedules/me` returns bare ticket IDs (`day-plan-query.service.ts:59-66`), so the M3 Ticket Detail screen has no data source (install tickets *are* SE-readable, `install.controller.ts:216` — a straight asymmetry); SEs also can't list their own vouchers or leave requests. (2) **An SE cannot log in** — `InMemoryUserStore` is a hardcoded 8-user array with exactly ONE SE (`user-store.ts:25-65`); beyond #91's durability story, `validateCredentials` uses **`scryptSync`** (`:78`) so every login blocks the event loop (~10–20 logins/sec process-wide, stalling all other traffic), the refresh Map never evicts consumed records (`refresh-token-store.ts:20,35` — unbounded growth), there is **no per-user revocation** (device loss unhandleable) and **no device identity anywhere** (zero `device_token`/`fcm`/`apns` columns in schema ⇒ push unaddressable even after #76). (3) **The process cannot hold the connections** — `PrismaPg` is constructed with only a connection string (`prisma.service.ts:28-37`), so the pool is node-postgres' default **max 10 with no acquisition timeout**, against live `statement_timeout=0` and `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=0` (#106 quantified); 1,000 pollers queue unboundedly with no error. Also: **`GET /me/shared-pool` is unbounded** (`shared-pool.service.ts:31-38`) — measured worst case **1,030 tickets / ~155 KB for one SE, per poll**; only **2 of ~14** SE mutations carry an idempotency key (troubleshoot + vouchers), and the 409/Shadow-Use path never persists `clientSubmissionId` (`troubleshoot-submission.service.ts:265-303`) so **every mobile retry re-decrements van stock** on top of #101's read-then-write lost update (`:315-320`); **`ZoneScopeGuard` is a no-op for SEs** (`zone-scope.guard.ts:27-29`) and `POST /tickets/:id/troubleshoot` checks no assignment/coverage (`:112-116`), so any SE can submit against any of the 9,280 open tickets fleet-wide; **offline is currently incompatible with verification** — writes are server-stamped on arrival (`:140`) while Phase 1 searches pings `gt: submittedAt` (`verification.service.ts:159`), so a late upload excludes the very pings proving the fix; delivery is **polling-only** (no WS/SSE/seam, #76 gateway has no adapter); correlation IDs exist **only in the exception filter** (`all-exceptions.filter.ts:37`) so successful requests are untraceable. **Positive findings:** intraday accept is the reference implementation (ownership + true retry-idempotency + atomic claim, `intraday-insertion.service.ts:139-160`); recovery/VU ownership correctly enforced; **zero SE-facing advisory-lock contention** (all `try_` variants, none on request paths). Deliverable `docs/status/backend-mobile-readiness-2026-07-22.md` — sections 1–10 incl. a ranked top-10 and 8 HITL decisions (push provider, offline strategy, token lifetime, one-device-vs-many, capture-time authority, day-plan acceptance, shared-pool write scope, multi-instance target). Assessment only; nothing filed. | this commit |
| 2026-07-22 | **Feasibility: inactive devices ranked by customer business criticality — READ-ONLY analysis (no code, no issue, no design).** Can we rank broken devices by whether the customer is actively dispatching that truck (`ap_widgets.tb_vehiclemaster.TRIP_CREATION_DATETIME`)? **YES, and the data is already in FSM** — `device_states.trip_creation_datetime` has been maintained on the 30-min telemetry tick since 2026-07-17, and the one design risk that could have killed it is absent: `AutoPlantSourceReader` pages on the **immutable `device_id` with no GPS-recency predicate and no cross-run cursor** (`autoplant-source-reader.ts:8-25,84-90`), and `upsertDeviceStates` is called with **every** chunk row independent of the `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` journal skip (`snapshot-ingestion.service.ts:77`) — so **inactive devices are still re-read and still refreshed every run**. Verified live against production (bounded `SELECT`+`LIMIT≤90`): 4/4 devices match FSM **to the second** rendered `AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'`, independently re-confirming SYSTEM-STATE §3b's two-different-offsets design (`latest_gps_datetime` DATETIME/IST +330 vs `TRIP_CREATION_DATETIME` TIMESTAMP/already-UTC offset 0). *Methodology warning recorded in the doc:* a naive comparison shows a clean +5:30 that is a **probe artifact** (mysql2 without `dateStrings` reinterpreting in node's IST locale, plus an ad-hoc PrismaClient omitting `prisma.service.ts:36`'s `-c timezone=UTC` so Postgres defaulted to `Asia/Calcutta`) — anyone re-running must pin both sessions or they will "find" a 5.5h bug that isn't there. **Quantified (full 2,729-device population, not a sample):** HIGH (trip ≤24h) **111 (4.1%), 17 with no SE assigned**, avg **96 days** inactive · MEDIUM 984 · LOW 1,287 · NO_TRIP_DATA 347; all have open tickets, so the gap is purely **ordering**. **Headline justifying the feature: business criticality is orthogonal to the SLA bucket the engine sorts by — 84 of 111 HIGH devices sit in `LONG_PENDING`, which the canonical sort ranks LAST**, while 658 devices with no trip in >7d ARE formally assigned; tier can't be proxying for it either (top-8 HIGH companies are all SILVER). Inactive vehicles are dispatched ~4× less than fleet average (4.7%/day vs 18.4%), so the signal discriminates. **Shape:** zero schema change (`device_states` already denormalises vehicle/plant/company/transporter/sla_bucket/inactivity_hours), **cached not live** (live would need ~31 paged VPN round-trips per unfiltered view under the <100-row cap; cached costs **zero** extra AutoPlant queries), dedicated ZM-scoped page, sort HIGH → unassigned → longest-inactive. **Recommender scoring seam: LATER, not now** — evidence is strong but gated on (a) unconfirmed semantics, (b) **#124** (a new weight wouldn't appear in `config_snapshot`, un-retrofittable), (c) the `f0f3dcb` per-zone-knobs governance decision; earn it by shipping the view and checking whether ZM manual picks correlate. **Caveats reported honestly:** `active_trip_id` dates disagree with the stamp on several prod rows ⇒ the column reads more like "active-trip record last written" than "trip created" (label operationally, confirm with AutoPlant owners); 86% of stamps fall in 2026-07 so LOW means "no dispatch in a fortnight", not "seasonal"; `GREATEST` monotonicity (`snapshot-ingestion.service.ts:122`) means a downward source correction can never propagate; and freshness currently depends on a human since `INGESTION_SCHEDULER_ENABLED="false"`. Deliverable `docs/analysis/inactive-devices-by-business-priority-2026-07-22.md` (verdict + evidence + 6 HITL decisions). Also noted: real trip **history** is sourceable later from `ap_widgets.tb_tripmaster` (`trip_created_date`/`trip_start_date`/`trip_status`) if last-value proves too coarse. Probe scripts deleted; no writes to AutoPlant or FSM. | this commit |
| 2026-07-22 | **Feasibility: inactive-device prioritization + last-known-location — READ-ONLY analysis (no code, no issue, no design).** Extends the same-day business-criticality analysis with the geolocation half. **YES to both; the location half is the cheapest of the two because FSM already ingests the coordinates and nobody noticed** — `AutoPlantSourceReader` has always selected `latitude, longitude` into `raw_device_snapshots.lat/lon` (`mapping.ts:143-144`): **2,769 of 2,771 inactive devices (99.93%) already have last-ping coordinates in FSM, and the stored ping timestamp matches `device_states.latest_gps_datetime` for 2,769 of 2,769**. Confirmed AutoPlant columns `latitude`/`longitude` (double), `current_location` (longtext reverse-geocoded address w/ offset), `vehicle_location_status` (SCHEDULED/ATPLANT/TOWARDSDESTINATION/EMPTY). **Corrected a premise in the brief:** AutoPlant's lat/lng does NOT update independently of pings — measured FSM last-ping vs AP live position over 30 inactive devices, **29/30 identical to the metre (0 m drift)**; the one 3,066 m exception had an AP GPS timestamp ~26 h NEWER, i.e. the truck resumed reporting (second case confirmed at ~29 h/85 m). So read-through would not drift for a *silent* device. **Snapshotting is still right, for two better reasons:** (1) **recovery** — 2 of 30 sampled devices resumed within a day, and read-through would silently swap "where we lost it" for "where it is now" exactly while an SE is en route; (2) **retention** — `raw_device_snapshots` holds history only by accident: `PARTITION_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED="false"`, so **591,033 rows are piled in `raw_device_snapshots_default`** and the newest daily partition is `y2026m07d10` (today 07-22) — the exact activation-checklist failure mode; fixing it (mandated paired with the ingestion scheduler) starts dropping daily partitions at `telemetry_retention_days=7` and **deletes the last-known location of everything inactive >7d**, while HIGH-bucket devices average ~182 days dark. **Recommended shape:** extend `device_states` (not a side table — precedent is `trip_creation_datetime`, added there 07-17; it already denormalises vehicle/plant/company/transporter/sla_bucket) with `last_known_lat/lng/address/location_at` + `vehicle_location_status`; **write-on-ping, not write-on-inactivity-transition** — same value ("location at last ping" IS "location when it went silent"), no transition detection, no flapping edge cases, correct on recovery, and it reuses the existing `unnest` upsert (`snapshot-ingestion.service.ts:114-123`, called for every chunk row per `:77`) — but **NOT** `GREATEST` for coordinates (last-observed-value, guarded on the ping advancing). Only the address + trip-state need a sync change (2 columns on an existing SELECT, zero extra AutoPlant queries); `trip_creation_datetime` already rides the 30-min tick and should **not** be moved to master sync as the brief proposed. **30-device sample (10/bucket):** 30/30 resolved in AP with a usable address; HIGH devices avg **4,355 h ≈ 182 days** dark and 9/10 `LONG_PENDING` (reproducing the orthogonality headline on an independent sample); **all 10 HIGH carried `vehicle_location_status='SCHEDULED'`**, reinforcing the "active-trip record last written" semantics; **three co-located device pairs in 30 rows** (Pune / Gurgaon / Banda — metres apart, one SE visit clears two tickets), which `plant_id` clustering cannot see. **Seams:** business-priority→scoring stays LATER (unchanged gates: semantics, #124, `f0f3dcb` governance); **location→distance scoring is a shorter path than a new weight** — the `distance` component already exists and is weighted 0.1 in `priority_rule_config` v1 but sits inert for want of input (`recommender.service.ts:371`), and device coordinates supply half of it (SE-side position still missing); coordinates are also the prerequisite for ever making `orderPlantStops` (`batch-assignment.service.ts:236-238`) route-aware. Also recommend surfacing last-known location on the existing Device Detail page (additive, no new endpoint) labelled "last known" with its timestamp. **Caveats:** address landmark offsets range 28 m–2.77 km (context, not navigation — lat/lng is truth); `vehicle_location_status` semantics sampled, not documented; a lat/lon backfill from `raw_device_snapshots` is possible **only until partition maintenance is fixed**. Deliverable `docs/analysis/inactive-device-priority-and-location-2026-07-22.md` (verdict per sub-feature + evidence + 7 HITL decisions). *Prod-query caution recorded:* an unbounded `GROUP BY` on `tb_vehiclemaster` times out — indexed `device_id` lookups only. Probe scripts deleted; no writes to AutoPlant or FSM. | this commit |

| 2026-08-04 | **[#204](./issues/204-time-semantics-day-boundary-implementation.md) finished — leave/availability windows and the admin planner now read the IST day; all six ACs met.** Picked up `204-HANDOFF.md` (now consumed → `docs/archive/`) and built the two items it left. **B8 (leave windows):** `istWindowStart`/`istWindowEnd` join the two day helpers in `src/common/ist-day.ts`. A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` names an **IST calendar day**, so it resolves to `[IST midnight of that date, IST midnight of the *next* date)` — the `+1 day` on the end is not a flourish, it is what makes the named day covered, because the active-window predicate is `windowStart <= now AND windowEnd > now` (`se-availability.service.ts:45,73`), i.e. **end-exclusive**. Wired into both write points that take a free-text window — `leave-request.controller.ts` (mobile sends date-only, `LeaveRequestFormScreen.tsx:46`) and `engineers.controller.ts :seId/availability` (mobile's field is free text, so date-only is reachable there too). Anything that is not a bare date passes to `new Date` untouched: admin's `datetime-local` is already `toISOString()`d (`SeManagementPage.tsx:89`) and is a real instant, not an IST calendar day. Two consequential behaviour changes, both falling out of end-exclusivity rather than chosen: `WINDOW_ORDER` is now `end <= start` (date-only made a zero-length window newly reachable — an end date exactly one day before the start resolves to *exactly* the start, and a leave request granting zero unavailability is a silent no-op, not a success), and a non-existent date (`2026-02-31`) stays Invalid Date instead of letting `Date.UTC` roll it over, preserving the `INVALID_WINDOW` 400. **Admin planner:** `istIsoDate`/`addIsoDays` added to `src/lib/datetime.ts` (shared home, mirroring the backend's one-definition posture); `PlannerPage.tsx` derives its 7-day window from them instead of device-local `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate` — `planned_date` is a `@db.Date` bucketed on the IST day, so a ZM planning at 02:00 IST was writing intents onto the previous day's column unless their machine was set to IST. **B7 went live and was fixed in the same slice — the issue predicted this exact thing** ("out of scope *unless the ruling makes one live*"). Once a window is stored as the instants bounding its IST days, `iso.slice(0, 10)` renders a start **one day early**: `LeaveRequestsPage.tsx:48`, `SeManagementPage.tsx:286-287` and mobile `leaveDisplay.ts:28-30` all did that. Replaced with a named start/end pair on both clients (`istWindowStartDate`/`istWindowEndDate`; `formatLeaveWindowStart`/`formatLeaveWindowEnd`) — the **end** helper steps back a millisecond before taking the IST date, because the stored end is exclusive and the raw instant names the day *after* the last covered one. Duplicated per app rather than lifted into `@fsm/shared` on purpose: that package ships built `dist/`, so a runtime helper there couples every consumer's test run to a rebuild step. TDD red→green throughout: the leave e2e failed `expected 'AVAILABLE' to be 'ON_LEAVE'` at 00:15 IST first, which is the B8 bug stated exactly. The planner test **forces the device zone to UTC** for its render cases — on an IST workstation the old code gives the right answer by accident and the test would have proven nothing. Verification: full backend suite + `tsc --noEmit`; admin 92 files / 414 tests + `tsc --noEmit`; mobile 46 suites / 313 tests + `tsc --noEmit`. **Pre-existing failure found, NOT caused by this work and not fixed here:** `voucher-controller.e2e-spec.ts` fails 2 tests in a full run and 3 in isolation — it has no fixture of its own for the seeded `se.north@fsm.test` and depends on whichever earlier spec last created that `engineer_master` row (and with which zone). Proven pre-existing by re-running it with this slice's backend files reverted to `5afc920`: byte-identical failure. **The analytics-day open question was put to the operator and RULED: move analytics to the IST day and recompute**, accepting rewritten history for the affected range — landed as a CONTEXT.md §19 addendum and filed as [#214](./issues/214-analytics-day-ist-recompute.md), which requires a written finding on each of the four unaudited cubes before any recompute runs. **#204 now has nothing open on it.** **Still open, unchanged and deliberately not decided here:** the analytics day is still UTC (`business-sweep-scheduler.service.ts:89`'s own `previousUtcDayStart`) while operations are now IST — three options written up on #204, needs an operator ruling, and the other four cubes remain unaudited. | `c84cb2b` + this commit |
| 2026-08-04 | **[#213](./issues/213-configurable-dispatch-schedule.md) DONE — the dispatch schedule becomes operator-owned configuration, and the overlap guard becomes real.** Four slices, each red→green. **(1) Schedule.** `system_settings.dispatch_cron` is the source of truth; `BUSINESS_SWEEP_DISPATCH_CRON` seeds the row once (create-only, so a redeploy never clobbers an operator's setting) and is never read again. A write validates → persists → re-points the **live** job, proven by the registered job's next fire moving 23:30→00:30 UTC *inside one process*. **Notable:** `cron` was NOT added as a dependency — `@nestjs/schedule` v4 doesn't re-export it and it isn't resolvable from `apps/backend`, so `dispatch-cron.ts` takes the `CronTime` constructor off a live job. That began as lockfile avoidance (the lock carries another session's uncommitted state) but is the better answer anyway: **the parser that validates an operator's expression is byte-for-byte the parser that will run it** — a separately-versioned copy could accept an expression the scheduler then rejects, which is precisely the accepted-then-silently-dead schedule AC-4 exists to prevent. The `@Cron` decorator survives, but only to *register* the job under a stable name/timezone: it evaluates once at class-decoration time, long before a DB is reachable, so `DispatchScheduleService.onApplicationBootstrap` re-points it (bootstrap, not module-init — `@nestjs/schedule` mounts decorator jobs in its own bootstrap hook). **A hole closed alongside:** `PUT /api/settings/:key` is OH-only but writes *any* key — left open it bypasses both guarantees at once (unparseable value stored AND the job never re-registered, so the schedule reads as changed while dispatch fires at the old hour). `SettingsService.set` now refuses keys with a specialised writer and names the endpoint that owns them. **(2) Guard.** The scheduler's private `inFlight` field is **deleted**; the guard lives inside `runForActiveZones`, the one path the cron tick and the manual trigger share, so neither can bypass it — the exact defect the issue was filed for. `runForActiveZones` returns `RAN | CONFLICT` (a union, not an exception: a refusal is a first-class answer, and the union forces every future caller to acknowledge it); six existing call sites narrowed via a shared `expectRan` helper rather than loosened. The operator-requested regression case passes — scheduled run in flight + manual trigger → exactly one run *and* a populated 409 naming the zone, the start time in IST and the actor. **Stated honestly on the issue:** the guard is per-zone and **in-process**; it is what gives an operator a clear answer, not a distributed lock — the cross-process guarantee remains the advisory locks + idempotency (#100). **(3) Ledger reason** — migration `20260804150000_dispatch_run_reason`, blank stored as null not `''`, surfaced in run detail. **(4) Admin** — Settings › Dispatch Schedule tab (shows timezone + next fire, so an operator can confirm the change *took*), and the Run-dispatch button disables itself with the reason while a run is in flight, polled because the run it guards against is usually the cron starting unprompted. **Deliberately not done:** other sweep crons stay env-configured (did not fall out for free — each needs its own key, seed, validation route and re-registration hook); no range restriction on the expression (`* * * * *` is valid and accepted — narrowing what is *sensible* is a product question #213 doesn't rule on). **Dev DB needs `pnpm prisma migrate deploy`** for the new column. Verification: admin 93 files / 420 tests + `tsc` clean; backend `tsc` clean; full backend suite green apart from the pre-existing `voucher-controller` failure documented on the #204 line above. | `5bf1c02` + this commit |

switches, **not** by missing code. "Code" = mechanism present & tested; "Data" = the dev/prod DB lacks
the rows the stage consumes; "Paused" = an audited ops toggle deliberately left OFF.

| Ticket creation (inactive+eligible → OPEN ticket) | #112 | ✅ done (`integration-sync.service.ts:78→80`, `:130→132`) | **Paused (business)** — `eligibility_mode='pgi'` over empty `pgi_history` (B7) → 0 eligible → 0 ticket-candidates today. Empty `engineer_master`/`se_coverage` still → UNASSIGNABLE, but the decision "where do SEs come from" is resolved: admin-entered, no feed/seed |

**Root blockers, ranked:** (1) engineers/coverage data — a *tested* seed script would unblock the pending
decision without taking it; (2) B7 eligibility decision; (3) the two ops toggles. All code seams exist.

### Activation checklist (env/ops enable order — do NOT flip casually)

The schedulers are OFF by default. When activating for real (a deliberate ops step, post zone
ratification), enable in this order and mind the couplings:

1. **`eligibility_mode`** (audited `system_settings`, OH-owned) — `pgi` (canonical) requires a live SAP
   PGI feed; until then the interim `all-deployed` proxy makes current-fitment-on-ACTIVE devices eligible.
   Harmless to set while schedulers are OFF (it only bites on the next pipeline recompute).
2. **`INGESTION_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=true`** — turns the pipeline self-running (masters daily + telemetry
   every 30 min). **MUST be enabled together with `PARTITION_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED=true`** — without it,
   after the 3-day partition create-ahead runway new pings silently fall into the DEFAULT partition and
   retention never runs (handoff §4 item 5 / `docs/archive/HANDOFF-autoplant-ingestion-2026-07-07.md`). Treat the
   two as one switch. Also set `INGESTION_STALE_RUN_MIN` above the telemetry cadence (reaper safety).
3. **`BUSINESS_SWEEPS_ENABLED=true`** — turns on dispatch (`business-dispatch` cron) + the 10 field-loop
   sweeps (verification / intraday-timeout / cross-zone / install-verification / …). Needs SE + coverage
   data present (else every ticket is UNASSIGNABLE) — SEs are admin-entered via `/engineers/manage`.
   **SECOND SWITCH PAIR — sweeps depend on ingestion (#148, 2026-07-22).** The verification and
   install-activation sweeps resolve a 24-hour window against `raw_device_snapshots`, so they are only
   meaningful while step 2 is actually running. **This pair is now ENFORCED IN CODE**, not just
   documented: both sweeps refuse to expire a window until the telemetry watermark
   (`snapshot_runs.data_as_of`) has advanced past the submission / activation
   (`VerificationService.windowExpired`, `InstallLifecycleService.activationWindowExpired`). Before
   #148 a submission made while ingestion was paused aged into an **irreversible**
   `FAILED_VERIFICATION` / `FAILED_ACTIVATION` — rolling back `PRE_VERIFICATION` inventory and pushing
   a false failure to the SE — regardless of whether the SE had fixed the device.
   **Consequence to watch:** the guard converts a wrong verdict into a window that stays PENDING
   indefinitely while telemetry is frozen. That is the correct trade (it can only ever delay a failure,
   never cause one), but it must be **visible** — surfacing stalled windows on `/build-health` is
   #148 slice 3, still open. **Never** "fix" a stalled window by auto-expiring after a grace period;
   that re-creates the original bug with a longer fuse.

> **Note on the state of these flags today (2026-07-22):** the checklist above describes the *enable
> order*, not current reality. `apps/backend/.env` currently has `BUSINESS_SWEEPS_ENABLED="true"` with
> `INGESTION_SCHEDULER_ENABLED="false"` and `PARTITION_MAINTENANCE_ENABLED="false"` — i.e. **step 3 is
> on while step 2 is off**, exactly the inversion the pairing above warns about. That is what made
> #148 an armed defect rather than a hypothetical one, and it is why the pairing is now enforced in
> code. Corrected in `SYSTEM-STATE` by #149.

Manual HTTP triggers (`POST /api/integration/run-pipeline`, `POST /api/schedules/dispatch-run`, the
per-sweep triggers) drive the exact same code paths **without** enabling any cron — use them for watched
runs while the flags stay OFF.

The guard is **the status that caller read**, not an enumerated from-list — `escalateFraud` legitimately acts on `FAILED_VERIFICATION`, written by the very `finalize` it races, so a "not terminal" guard would have broken the door's primary flow. - 303 — [Dispatch day survives a crash between tick claim and admission](./issues/303-dispatch-tick-claim-crash-gap.md) → RC-3, W2/P2 — **DONE 2026-09-02** (`docs/progress/303-dispatch-tick-claim-crash-gap.md`): **no schema change** — neither design the issue offered was needed. Grace = #260 retry deadline + stale-run threshold (25 min), because a patient tick legitimately holds a claim with no run for the whole deadline (#259 writes no run while every zone is held). Scoped to today's IST day: `markZonesForRecovery` stamps `businessDate = istDate(now)`, so acting on an older claim would mark today's zones for a day that is over — and the dev DB already holds 5 such claims.

No transaction holds an engineer lock and then asks for a zone lock ⇒ no cycle; contention on one engineer is a queue while every other engineer in both zones proceeds. Surplus is the `processing_rank` **suffix**, named `CAPACITY_REACHED`. Caught a stale assertion: `dispatch-per-se-isolation`'s throughput case offered 40 tickets to a capacity-20 SE and asserted all 160 landed — it now seeds a capacity above `PER_SE`, since it measures the transaction budget, not the capacity guard.
- 305 — [Heartbeat inside the zone loop](./issues/305-dispatch-heartbeat-inside-zone-loop.md) → RC-5, W2/P2 *(per-SE beat; seq)* — **DONE 2026-09-02** (`docs/progress/305-dispatch-heartbeat-inside-zone-loop.md`): an optional `onProgress` beat on both long phases — `dispatchForZone` per SE (strictly BETWEEN transactions; a beat inside one that later rolls back never happened) and `runForZone` every 50 tickets, since recommendation is the half that scales with ticket count (AR-11 fan-out). `DISPATCH_STALE_RUN_MIN` untouched — a bigger blind window is not a beat — and the write is still guarded on `status: 'RUNNING'`, so a reaped run cannot beat itself back to life.

- 310 — [Mutation-door input validation](./issues/310-mutation-door-input-validation.md) → CB-3+CB-9+past-dates, W3/P2 — **DONE 2026-09-02** (`docs/progress/310-mutation-door-input-validation.md`): `OverrideCommandDto` on both override doors (the body was an *interface*, and the global pipe skips those by design, so nothing validated the one door whose contract says "mandatory reason"). It deliberately does **not** enumerate `action` — an unimplemented action is a deploy-ordering problem and the service's `UNSUPPORTED_ACTION` names it, where an `@IsIn` would blame the client; both halves pinned. Uuids validated as **Postgres** accepts them (8-4-4-4-12 hex), not as RFC 4122 defines them: `@IsUUID`'s version nibble would refuse ids this repo's own specs use, and did, on the first green run. New `common/parse-id.ts` returns `null` rather than throwing — whether a malformed id is a 404 or a 400 is a question about the resource, not the parse — and is stricter than `BigInt`, which reads `''` as `0n` and `'0x1f'` as `31n`. New `INVALID_DATE` outcome on both writers rather than reusing `TARGET_DATE_IN_PAST`: a move onto today is legal, a defer to today is not (`notDeferredOn` is inclusive, so it dispatches again immediately). **The suite's real find was not an over-strict DTO but seven spec files deferring/holding into the past** — each passing a date future relative to its own fixture clock and never passing that clock to the writer, so the tests proving deferral works were exercising RC-11's silent no-op; `placeHold` had no injectable clock at all and now takes one in its options bag. - 319 — [Same-day recovery for zones lost to contained errors](./issues/319-recovery-symmetry-contained-errors.md) → AR-13, W3/P3 — **DONE 2026-09-02** (`docs/progress/319-errored-zone-same-day-recovery.md`): recovery pointed the wrong way round — kill the process and the zone was marked, re-dispatched and reported; let a zone throw *inside* a live run and the ledger recorded ERROR and nothing asked for that zone again until 05:00 tomorrow. **What marks is now a claim finalizing ERROR, not the cause of it** — both losses end at the same `dispatch_run_zones` row in the same state — so `processZone` (a contained throw, or a whole-zone `skipReason`) and `releaseStrandedClaims` (a claim still open as the run unwinds, the half the reaper structurally cannot reach) both write the reaper's own `markZonesForRecovery`, **verbatim**: one row, one budget, one cutoff per (zone, day) however many ways the zone was lost, and no new state member, no collector change, no migration. Both mark **before** finalizing/freeing — the reaper's ordering rule: a death in the gap leaves the claim RUNNING, exactly what the next reap pass finds. `releaseStrandedClaims` had to start reading (a blind `updateMany` cannot name what it frees) and now takes the run's `now`, so a mark written while unwinding lands on the day the run was dispatching. **The interaction checked rather than assumed:** the collector re-dispatches through `runForActiveZones`, so a failing recovery run re-marks the zone from inside the collector's own attempt — safe because the mark write never touches `attempts`, keeping the collector's `{state:'PENDING', attempts:<seen>}` guard matching and the budget spending once per attempt; pinned by a test. DONE zones are never marked and CONTENDED rows come from `admit`, which neither writer goes through, so #286's "busy is not broken" holds by construction. **UI (the issue's "coverage widens"):** the notice said "this zone's dispatch run **died**", false for both new cases (the run finished and reported the loss) and enough to send an operator hunting a crashed process that never existed — it now says the zone *lost its dispatch run* and leaves the cause to `last_error`, with a new admin test asserting it never says "died".

Both numbers are therefore **read back the way `DayPlanQueryService` reads them** (new shared `liveBatchFilter`), not derived from the transaction's own bookkeeping: `stopSequence` is a numbering rather than a count, and a stop whose every ticket was withdrawn is not on the plan at all (#179 slice 3), so the cheap derivation over-reports twice after a ZM removal. - 278 — [The SE detail panel can show an earlier day's plan as "today's"](./issues/278-engineer-detail-current-schedule-no-date-predicate.md) → 269, 147  *(filed 2026-08-20 from #269's build, and deliberately not folded into it. `EngineersQueryService.currentDayPlan` and `currentAssignments` resolve "the SE's current schedule" as `findFirst({ seId, liveScheduleFilter() }, orderBy: dispatchedAt desc)` with **no date predicate**, so a still-`ACTIVE` plan from an earlier day is a legitimate match and, if it sorts first, is presented as today's — ticket count, schedule dates and every plant stop from the wrong day. Exactly the defect #147 fixed for the SE's own Day Plan, where the fix carries the reasoning verbatim: "the date predicate, not the ordering, decides which plan is today's". #269 closed the **capacity** half of this on the same service — `activeTicketCount` is now date-scoped through the shared `committedDayLoad` and agrees with the recommender — but this neighbouring read is not a capacity question: it is *which schedule is current*, and answering it means ruling on what a genuinely multi-day plan should show and whether "no plan today" should render as empty (the SE's own Day Plan's answer) or as stale work labelled with its own dates. A small design call rather than a drive-by, and #269 carried no AC over it. #178's closure recycle shrinks the stale population but does not remove the case; this is the defence that does not depend on a sweep having run. Pinning it needs the older schedule given the **later** `dispatchedAt`, so ordering alone cannot produce the right answer.)*
- 257 — **✅ DONE 2026-08-20 (`16dbc9c`), filed and fixed in one session.** [The stored dispatch schedule is never applied at boot](./issues/257-dispatch-schedule-never-applied-at-boot.md) -> 213  *(filed 2026-08-20 from a scheduler-engine analysis that took seriously the ERROR line opening **every** e2e app boot — hundreds of boots across three suite runs, 100% of them: `stored dispatch schedule '0 5 * * *' could not be applied … No Cron Job was found (business-dispatch)`. Root cause is framework hook ordering: `@Cron` jobs are only **mounted** into `SchedulerRegistry` by `SchedulerOrchestrator`'s own `onApplicationBootstrap`, and Nest runs bootstrap hooks deepest-module-first (`b.distance - a.distance`), which on this graph puts `DispatchScheduleService`'s hook **before** the mount — so `getCronJob` threw on every boot and the job stayed on the compile-time default. Invisible only because the seeded value equals the default: the day an operator changes the dispatch hour, the next restart silently reverts dispatch to 05:00 IST while the API reports the stored value — #213's guarantee held within a process and broke across processes. Fixed with the ordering Nest actually guarantees rather than a graph massage: `applyStoredSchedule()` called from `main.ts` after `app.listen()`; the bootstrap hook seeds the row and applies only behind `registry.doesExist`, logging at `log` when it defers. Pinned by `dispatch-schedule-boot.e2e-spec.ts`, which writes `0 6 * * *` BEFORE booting — the restart scenario the existing #213 test could not see, since its stored value equalled the default and the assertion passed whether the apply ran or not.)*
- 256 — **✅ DONE 2026-08-20 (`bd7dd06`).** [`plant-zone-change-impact` fails every night between 00:00 and 05:30 IST](./issues/256-plant-zone-change-impact-utc-ist-day-fixture.md) -> 107, 204  *(filed 2026-08-20 from #255's second verification run, and **not** caused by it. Two full suites on the same tree disagreed: the 18:03 IST run gave the known 2 failures, the 23:33 IST run gave 3. The extra one reproduces **in isolation**, so it is neither a fixture collision nor #184 — it is the clock. `zone-mapping.service.ts:209` reads the **IST** day (`istDate(new Date())`, #204's ruling, correctly applied) while the spec's fixture stamps its `work_schedules` row with `setUTCHours(0,0,0,0)`, a **UTC** day. IST is UTC+05:30, so for the 5.5 hours from 00:00 to 05:30 IST the two name different dates, `dateTo >= day` misses, and `dispatchedTodayCount` is 0 instead of 1; the other 18.5 hours it passes. Confirmed against the clock at the failing isolation run — 05:13 IST / 23:43 UTC. **This is the third distinct non-regression reason a full run can be red**, after `voucher-controller` (#187) and the #184 crash, and it is the one that matters most for **#107**: a nightly CI schedule lands squarely inside the failing window. Fix is the fixture, plus a sweep of `setUTCHours(0, 0, 0, 0)` across `test/` for the same UTC-vs-IST mismatch — #204's own session found two, this is a third. Pinning it needs care: the host runs on IST, so the naive test cannot tell the two apart for most of the day.)*
- 255 — **✅ DONE 2026-08-19 (`def334b`).** [16 e2e files share one hardcoded SE id and race on a partial unique Prisma cannot see](./issues/255-shared-se-fixture-races-partial-unique.md) -> 107  *(filed 2026-08-19 from the #247-#249 full-suite verification. The run reported 4 failed files; only the known `voucher-controller` pair was real — the other three (`soft-state-controller`, `ticket-forms-read`, `troubleshoot-controller`) threw in **`beforeAll`**, so **zero** of their tests ran, and all three pass 3/3 in isolation. Root cause is exact: sixteen e2e files hardcode `SE_ID = '22222222-…-222222222222'` (the in-memory auth seed) and each upserts a **DEDICATED** `se_coverage` row for it at its **own** plant. The upsert's conflict target is `(se_id, plant_id)` — different plants, no conflict, so both INSERT — but `20260618121101…/migration.sql:60` also declares `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX se_coverage_dedicated_se_key ON se_coverage(se_id) WHERE coverage_type = 'DEDICATED'`, a **partial** unique that is raw SQL by necessity and therefore invisible to the Prisma client. The loser is rejected. Structural, not incidental: all sixteen use DEDICATED and their own plant, so whether it fires is purely which files a worker pool runs concurrently. A second, deterministic bug rides along — `afterAll` deletes `engineer_master` before `se_coverage` and violates `se_coverage_se_id_fkey`. **Why it matters:** a suite-level `beforeAll` throw reports zero tests, so those files silently contribute no coverage on a colliding run; every red run needs hand-triage into "real" vs "collided", which is precisely the triage cost that made an earlier session wrongly indict its own change (#184 note); and **#107's unattended CI cannot hand-triage at all**. Preferred fix is the inverse of the obvious one: one DEDICATED coverage per SE is a real business invariant, so the partial index is right and sixteen files each asserting their own is the mistake — seed it once in global setup rather than per file.)*
- 254 — **✅ DONE 2026-08-20 (`16dbc9c`).** [`plant-eligibility-refresh` fires *after* the dispatch it feeds (unpinned cron, #240 family)](./issues/254-plant-eligibility-refresh-cron-unpinned.md) -> 138, 240  *(filed 2026-08-19 while writing down the daily cron chain for #247 — found by documenting it, not by a test. `plant-eligibility-refresh-scheduler.service.ts:59` registers with **no `timeZone`**, and its own docstring states the bug while stating the intent: "04:30 **UTC**, i.e. shortly before the default 05:00 dispatch tick". That dispatch is 05:00 **IST** (23:30 UTC), so on a UTC host the refresh lands at 10:00 IST — five hours **after** the batch it exists to feed, which then consumes a `plant_eligible_floating_se` MV up to a day stale. Identical shape to the `schedule-closure` defect #240 fixed; that fix was scoped to two jobs and this one was not among them, and #247's new sweep was pinned from the start — so this is the last unpinned link. **Impact is bounded, not nil**: #138 slice 1 re-checks `coverage_type`/`is_active` live and slice 2 refreshes after each master sync, so this scheduler is the *backstop* — the effect is that the backstop's staleness bound is a day wider than intended on the plant-SE geometry the floating leg still reads from the MV. Fix is three lines plus a behavioural pin; **the pin must be verified under `TZ=UTC`**, because the dev host runs on IST and removing the option does not turn such a test red locally. Carries a fourth AC to rule explicitly on the report cubes' day/month boundaries, which are still UTC while the rest of the system reads days as IST.)*

- 222 — FSM shifts every GPS ping 5.5 h into the past (`AUTOPLANT_UTC_OFFSET_MIN` is wrong) → 223, 228  *(filed 2026-08-07 as reconciliation finding F2; **re-diagnosed 2026-08-07** by the blind PRISM read + `audit/cross-analysis.md`. **The original diagnosis on this issue was wrong and has been withdrawn in place.** It read "not a timezone bug — FSM’s conversion is correct, its data is old"; it is a timezone bug, the conversion is wrong, and the data was fresh. The 5.10 h median came from comparing FSM against the **Excel snapshot** (01:19 UTC) rather than the live source, 25 min before FSM’s own sync (01:45 UTC) — frozen devices give exactly **−5.50 h**, live devices 5.50 − 0:25 = **−5.10 h**, and the whole distribution is 27 min wide. The hard floor the issue itself reported as `min`/`p05` **was the signature**. `07:15 IST − 5:30 = 01:45 IST` — the "staleness" was the shift, to the minute; run 151 wrote 20,578 rows and was not an incomplete pass. **The source never changed either** (my own PRISM claim, also withdrawn): `raw_device_snapshots.gps_datetime` holds the post-conversion value, so per-run percentile lag time-travels the contract — **5.52–5.65 h flat across all 95 runs from 2026-07-07 to 2026-08-07**, no discontinuity. `+330` was wrong when written; the 2026-07-17 verification used fleet-wide `MAX()`, which is decided by **4 devices out of 56,564** that genuinely write IST. Re-measured impact: **434 falsely inactive (16.2% of the queue), all 434 holding an open TROUBLESHOOT ticket**, and 434 of the 665 `CRITICAL` devices fabricated (65% of the band).)*

- 228 — Every guard in this system is one-directional, and each fails toward "fine" → 218, 221, 222, 223, 217  *(filed 2026-08-07 from `audit/cross-analysis.md` §4 — the cross-cutting finding behind three defects found in two days. #218’s `@Optional()` cannot fail on absence; #223’s `healthy + inactive = operational` is a **tautology** (`reconciliation.service.ts:213` says so out loud) and has been green over 913 misclassified devices; #222’s skew guard rejects only the **future** while the bug travelled into the **past**. **Not the same bug** — a DI issue, a modelling gap, a contract error — but one shared failure *mode*: each guard was written against the failure the author imagined and could not fail in the direction the real one travelled. - 230 — A partial telemetry ingest silently manufactures fleet-wide inactivity; run 153 opened 3,439 phantom tickets → 229, 231, 228, 222  *(filed 2026-08-10 while diagnosing an operator report of "inaccurate data on the dashboard". **[MEASURED]** `POST /integration/run-pipeline` ran snapshot run **153**, which finalised **`PARTIAL` with all 29 chunks `SUCCESS`** — a combination reachable only through the `readError` branch (`snapshot-ingestion.worker.ts:109-118`), i.e. the AutoPlant scan **threw mid-drain** after 29 × 90 = **2,610 rows**. `DeviceStateService.recompute()` then ran across **all 27,032** mirrored devices anyway, so the **24,422 the read never reached** aged on wall-clock alone past the inactivity threshold; ticket creation opened **3,439** Failure Cycles, of which **3,425 (99.6%) are on devices run 153 never fetched telemetry for**. | 2026-08-05 | **[#209](./issues/209-mobile-build-pipeline-device-install.md) — the mobile app has a native Android build for the first time; NOT yet on a handset, so the issue stays open.** `./gradlew assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, `app-debug.apk` 58.4 MB, arm64-v8a, 22 native libs. **Autolinking resolved everything, including `react-native-keychain` and `react-native-community_netinfo`** — the biggest unknown in the plan. Whether the keychain *works* is still unproven: `adb devices` was empty for the whole session, so the two ACs carrying the actual value (installs+launches; `se.north@fsm.test` logs in and the session survives an app restart) are **blocked on hardware**, not deferred. **The build fight, because it will recur on any new machine:** five failures each hiding the next, and the root cause was not path length as it first appeared — **Android CMake 3.22.1 bundles ninja 1.10, whose manifest lacks `longPathAware`**, so it is hard-capped at 260 chars regardless of the registry. Fix is `sdkmanager "cmake;3.31.6"` (ninja 1.12.1, long-path aware), pinned in `android/build.gradle`. Path shortening alone provably cannot work: **175 of the 319 characters are immovable React Native codegen structure**, so even `nodeLinker: hoisted` + a 2-char repo root lands ~272. Kept as margin (each independently justified): `LongPathsEnabled=1` (machine registry, admin — **cannot live in the repo, so a fresh clone without it fails identically**), `-DCMAKE_OBJECT_PATH_MAX=1024`, `buildStagingDirectory → C:/x/<module>`, `virtualStoreDir: C:/pv` + `virtualStoreDirMaxLength: 40` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (chosen over `nodeLinker: hoisted` to keep pnpm's isolated linking, so phantom deps still fail loudly in backend/admin), and `reactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a` (armeabi-v7a is 2 chars longer and overflowed; also ~4x faster, and `expo run:android` builds one ABI anyway). Two dead ends recorded in-file so nobody retries them: relocating modules' Gradle `buildDir` (RN's `Android-autolinking.cmake` reads the *project* dir, not the build dir) and raising `CMAKE_OBJECT_PATH_MAX` alone. **`apps/mobile/android/` is now TRACKED**, deliberately against Expo's CNG advice — the `build.gradle` block can't be a config plugin and would be silently wiped; `expo prebuild --clean` is banned in the runbook. Also landed: netinfo **12.0.1 → 11.4.1 pinned exactly** (backs `connectivity.ts`, which #186 depends on), expo 54.0.35 → 54.0.36, `expo install --check` clean; a root `ErrorBoundary` (TDD, 6 tests) mounted **outside** `AuthProvider` so a keychain-rehydrate throw is caught; `.env.example` + runbook covering both networking routes — `adb reverse` (recommended: no LAN IP, no firewall rule) and LAN IP (**verified no inbound rule for TCP 3000 exists and all three profiles default inbound to Block**, so that route would fail as a timeout resembling a wrong URL). Mobile suite 47 suites / 319 tests green; `tsc` clean. **Raised, not folded in:** `android.permission.CAMERA` is absent from the generated manifest while `InstallFormScreen.tsx:43` and `VoucherFormScreen.tsx:55` call `launchCameraAsync` (`expo-image-picker` missing from `app.json` plugins) — photo capture will fail on device; **needs a follow-up issue**. Runbook: `docs/runbooks/mobile-android-build.md`. | `fd289de` |
| 2026-08-05 | **[#216](./issues/216-mobile-camera-permission-missing-from-manifest.md) filed — `android.permission.CAMERA` is absent from the generated manifest, so BOTH photo flows are dead on a handset.** Found by [#209](./issues/209-mobile-build-pipeline-device-install.md)'s first native build and deliberately not fixed there. `expo-image-picker` is missing from `app.json`'s `plugins`, so its config plugin never injects the permission — and **Android will not grant a runtime permission the manifest never declared**, so `requestCameraPermissionsAsync()` returns `granted: false` with no system dialog at all. Both call sites then bail to a bare `CAMERA_PERMISSION_DENIED` with no in-app recovery (`VoucherFormScreen.tsx:48-52`, `InstallFormScreen.tsx:38-42`). Invisible to Jest and `tsc` — every test mocks `expo-image-picker`, and the manifest is generated rather than authored. **This contradicts `audit/mobile-device-readiness-2026-08-04.md` in two places** (line 64 "Voucher and Install photos work"; line 159 Vouchers is "**the one screen you can exercise for real today**") — the audit read the source correctly but predates any APK, so it could not have checked the manifest. #216 therefore owns the audit correction as an AC, not just the one-line `app.json` fix, because the pilot readiness picture currently rests on that claim. | (uncommitted — filed with this commit) |

| 2026-08-05 | **Home dashboard brought up to `docs/ui/mobile/home-dashboard.png` — the missing chart is real now, not deferred ([#175](./issues/175-se-work-history-series.md) half-closed, [#55](./issues/55-mobile-home.md) parity).** Operator ask: "elements are missing like graphs". Built the one piece #172 decision 1 had explicitly shipped Home without. **Backend — `GET /api/me/work-history?days=N`** (`me-work-history.service.ts`, provider on `MeTicketsModule`, route on the existing `MeTicketsController`): dense oldest-first `[{date, assigned, completed}]`, `days` clamped 1–31 because a query value is an unvalidated string and a junk one must render a default chart, not 500 a working screen. **The source decision #175 said to settle before building:** assigned(D) = distinct tickets in the SE's batches on every schedule covering **IST** day D minus ZM-removed rows; completed(D) = of *that day's assigned set*, tickets with a `ticket_events` closure row inside day D. Read from the **event ledger, not `tickets.status`** — the status column says where a ticket ended up, never when, so "what did this SE complete on 09 May" is unanswerable from it once the ticket moves again; the ledger is also what a ZM's view of the same day reads, which is the AC that the two agree. `completed ⊆ assigned` is therefore true **by construction**, which is what lets a bar print `4/6` as a fraction and never overflow its track. Closure states are byte-identical to the KPI strip's COMPLETED tile — same screen, so a second definition would be visible as a contradiction. Spec pins the IST boundary with a closure at `2026-06-18T18:45Z` (00:15 IST on the 19th) that scores **0 under UTC bucketing**; also pins that the fixture cannot put one ticket live in two batches (partial-unique `(ticket_id) WHERE removed_at IS NULL`). **Mobile —** `WorkHistoryChart` (7 bars, `completed/assigned` label, date axis, two-series legend), `PlantWorkloadCard` (ring + meter + work/pending legend + ratio), `plantSummary.ts` (one derivation feeding **both** the Next-Visit subline and the workload cards, so the two cards cannot disagree about the same plant), branded header block with the Online / Last-sync chips. **Charts are plain Views on purpose:** `react-native-svg` ships native code, so adding it invalidates the installed debug APK and forces the [#209](./issues/209-mobile-build-pipeline-device-install.md) Android rebuild — it buys nothing a stacked rounded view can't draw. | 2026-08-30 | **Runtime fatal handlers — the backend can no longer die silently** (operator incident, 2026-08-28: *"navigating between pages … the application suddenly closed and took me to logout page"*). **Diagnosis first, from evidence rather than from the symptom:** the process was dead and the port free, and `cron_tick_claims` pinned the death to a **two-minute window (08:30–08:32Z)** — sweeps claiming without a gap up to `08:30`, then the `08:32/08:34/08:36/08:38` outbox ticks simply absent — i.e. **within two minutes of the hour's largest sweep batch (9 jobs aligning at `:30`), correlating with a timer, not with the page navigation the operator was doing**. Ruled out with measurements, not assumptions: OOM (93 MB working set / 297 MB peak under deliberate load), native crash (zero `node.exe` entries in Windows Error Reporting), Postgres restart or connection loss (`pg_postmaster_start_time()` = 2026-08-26 continuous, 6/100 connections), a #130 runtime-lock refusal (one consistent row), and the Console's own endpoints (`/dispatch/today`, `/changes-today`, `/action-required`, `/schedules?date=` and **six concurrent `/schedules/preview` recommender runs** — all 200, process survived). **The structural finding:** `runWithFatalGuard` (#98 leg 3) wraps `bootstrap()` **only**, so after `listen()` resolved *nothing* held `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` — on Node 18 one stray rejection from any of the ~20 `@Cron` sweeps or any request path killed the API **with no log line at all**, and `npm run start` (bare `node dist/main.js`) has no supervisor to bring it back. **Built TDD** (red 7/7 → green): `installFatalHandlers` in `src/bootstrap-guard.ts`, installed in `main.ts` **before** `bootstrap()` so a boot-time rejection is caught too — one FATAL line carrying the stack, a **bounded** `app.close()` (so Prisma `$disconnect` + the AutoPlant MySQL pool release, and a hung close cannot leave a zombie on port 3000), then exit 1. Also extracted `describeError`, because `unhandledRejection` hands through a *reason* that is usually not an `Error` and `String()` renders those `[object Object]` — as useless as the silence. **The lifecycle is deliberately unchanged**: Node already terminated on an unhandled rejection, and soldiering on would leave ~20 jobs *writing dispatch data* from an unvouched state — the hazard #130 exists to prevent. Surviving a crash is a supervisor's job, which is the open half → [#294](./issues/294-backend-silent-death-no-supervisor.md) (filed **needs-info**, not ready-for-agent: the line that names the cause did not exist when it crashed, and inventing a culprit from a 2-minute correlation is exactly the "status line is a hypothesis" failure this tracker warns about; it carries the two leads — fire-and-forget work escaping `runGuarded`, and the fact that the crashing `dist` was **built from a dirty tree carrying other sessions' WIP**, so the crash cannot be attributed to committed code). **Verified end to end, not only by unit test:** a real `process.on('unhandledRejection')` in a live node process now prints `FATAL [Bootstrap] Unhandled promise rejection — Error: … at …`, runs the graceful close, and exits 1, where before it printed nothing. 17 boot-related tests green (7 new + bootstrap-guard/boot-config/runtime-lock-boot); `tsc --noEmit` clean; backend rebuilt (`v1787902367`) and restarted on the fix (PID 2304, health 200) | this commit |

The day axis became **one optional argument** (`targetDay`), and the new `MOVE_TICKET` command rides every property the mover already guaranteed: the ticket is never `UNASSIGNED` in between (both rows in one transaction), `batch_assignment_tickets_one_active_per_ticket` makes a both-days duplicate impossible at the database, and `deferred_until` is never written. **Scheduler ownership needed no new flag** — the recommender selects `assignment_state = 'UNASSIGNED'`, so a moved ticket is not a candidate on its target day, and `batch-assignment.service.ts` *appends* to an existing live `(se, zone, date)` schedule (its own comment already names "a ZM_MANUAL plan").
